A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same gWorld models and MWMBench study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original world-model benchmarks, training-data scaling experiments, ablations, and downstream policy evaluations, with detailed results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds human evaluation and an analysis of performance on photographic GUI content.

M1.justification: The renderable-code prediction method, trajectory repurposing, image-to-code relabeling, look-ahead reasoning supervision, and Qwen3 VL backbones are unchanged. The appendix algorithms and prompts are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four training/in-distribution sources and the AndroidWorld and KApps evaluation sets. The human study samples existing benchmark examples, while the photographic-content analysis partitions existing test transitions; neither introduces new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The main benchmark and policy comparator sets remain unchanged. v2 adds an explicit latency comparison with VIMO's reported timing and an idealized variant in Table 7, without rerunning VIMO. The new photographic-content comparison uses seven existing baselines, omitting Llama 4 109B from that analysis.

E3.justification: Section 4.6 introduces a distinct human-assessment protocol: 100 examples weighted across six benchmarks, 12 annotators, and four anonymized predictions presented in randomized order alongside the reference transition. Section 4.7 adds content-stratified evaluation using Gemini 3 Flash classifications. These substantially extend evaluation procedures while leaving existing training and benchmark settings unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds two substantive diagnostic analyses absent from v1: whether automatic scores agree with human preferences, and whether photographic content undermines code-based world modeling. Sections 4.6–4.7 and Tables 4–5 directly test metric validity and a previously acknowledged representation limitation. Existing ablations, scaling analyses, and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The new human study explicitly reports three independent annotations per example, totaling 300 annotations, adding replication information for that assessment. No additional model-seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced; the existing appendix rank-correlation analyses remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, ablation, policy, and appendix scores are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial new findings. Human ranks are 1.68 and 2.16 for gWorld 32B and 8B, with human–automatic correlations of Spearman 0.806 and Kendall 0.600. Table 5 adds photographic/other IAcc scores of 74.98/79.68 for 32B and 75.26/75.92 for 8B. Table 7 newly totals generation and rendering as 1.30s and 0.55s, compared with reported VIMO timings.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, conditional transition objective, training-data constructions, and mathematical descriptions of look-ahead supervision and policy evaluation are unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical proofs, and the added empirical analyses supply no new formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions and claims concerning renderable-code world modeling, MWMBench, accuracy versus model size, data scaling, and downstream policy gains. The new conclusion restates these existing claims.

C2.justification: v1's Appendix E acknowledged photographic reconstruction limitations and conjectured limited semantic impact. v2 adds an interpretation of subgroup results supporting that conjecture and argues that structural GUI changes dominate benchmark difficulty. It also interprets the human study as validating its automatic metric; the original data-scale and memory limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies Gemini 3 Flash as the classifier used for the new content analysis and explicitly explains the generation-plus-rendering latency calculation. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, inference settings, prompts, and code/model/data access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive novelty positioning are retained. Updates to the Hoffmann scaling reference and Preference Leakage reference concern publication metadata for the same works. The expanded VIMO timing comparison supports the existing efficiency positioning.

P1.justification: v2 inserts two analysis subsections, expands the latency discussion, and adds a concluding paragraph and human-study acknowledgements. It also makes small terminology corrections. Most prose and the overall narrative structure, including the appendices, remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds human-evaluation, photographic-content, and latency tables. The former policy Table 4 becomes Table 6, and appendix tables are renumbered. Running title headers and local pagination change, while all existing figures and their substantive displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation by directly checking human agreement and testing the photographic-content limitation that v1 discussed largely as a conjecture. These additions make the retained findings better supported. The gain remains limited by the small human study without uncertainty bounds and a latency comparison based on reported VIMO timings rather than matched measurements.
